title: SDLC controls evidence record
description: One record per change: the tier, why that tier, what the tier required, and what this run actually verified. Emitted by `sdlc-controls tier --format json` and by `--evidence-out`.
x-stability: Major version 0 while the binary is 0.x. Fields may be added in any release, and additionalProperties is left open at every extension point so a pinned copy of this schema keeps validating newer documents; a consumer must ignore fields it does not recognise. Removing a field, renaming one, or narrowing what one means bumps the major to evidence/1. Closed sets that the algorithm itself fixes (the tier scale, the exit codes) stay closed. See docs/contract.md.

schema_version.description: Shape of this document. Versioned independently of the binary and of the policy binding.

change_id.description: PR/MR identifier, or <base>..<head> when none was supplied.

binding_used.description: Control binding the decision was made under, e.g. git-native-baseline@1.

affected_set.description: Component IDs the change touched, sorted.

unmatched_set.description: Changed paths that matched no component, sorted. A non-empty set drives the fail-safe floor.

reasons.description: Ordered decision trail; one entry per rule that fired, in the order the algorithm applied it. The order is meaningful.

controls_enforced.description: The tier's entry from the active policy: what the tier required, not what was checked. What was checked is in `verification`.

ai_assisted.description: CAF-SDLC-010. Whether any commit in the change declared AI assistance. A declaration, not a detection: false means nothing declared it.

ai_tool.description: CAF-SDLC-010. The tool named on the change.

ai_session.description: CAF-SDLC-010. Present only when exactly one session is declared; absent when the change spans several, because there is no single session to name.

prompt_ref.description: CAF-SDLC-010. Pointer to the issue or task.

accountable_approver.description: CAF-SDLC-011. The approver who satisfies segregation of duties. Absent when no approver set was available.

approver_ne_author.description: CAF-SDLC-011. Absent means NOT VERIFIED — never read an absent field as false.

approver_count.description: CAF-SDLC-011. Distinct approvers, folded case-insensitively. Absent means not verified; 0 means verified that nobody approved.

warnings.description: Prose form of everything this run could not settle: cross-repo consumers, stale-map hints, unverified controls. `verification` is the structured form.

map_version.description: `version` of the component map used. With `binding_used`, enough to reproduce the decision.

version.description: Binary version (SemVer). Moves independently of schema_version.

checks.description: Named checks the tier requires. This tool records them; the CI jobs the policy names execute them.

verification.description: What this run settled versus what it only recorded. The distinction is the point of the tool: a control that was not checked is never reported as passed.

approvers_supplied.description: Whether the run had an authoritative approver set. False means the approver controls were recorded, not checked.

verified.description: Control identifiers this run checked itself.

recorded_not_verified.description: Control identifiers recorded as required but enforced elsewhere — by the forge, by branch protection, or by the CI jobs the policy names.

controlId.description: Identifier of a control this run either settled or recorded. The set grows as controls are added, so a consumer must tolerate an identifier it does not recognise rather than reject the document. The values below are those evidence/0 defines today; they are examples, not a closed set.

pass.description: Whether the evidence settles every control it could check.

exit_code.description: The CLI's exit code alongside this record. A run that exits 2 produces no record, so only 0 and 1 appear here.

violations.description: Controls the evidence demonstrably fails. Empty when `pass` is true.
